The [Agent Gateway](https://pages.github.tools.sap/AI/agent-gateway-documentation) serves as the central communication hub for managing Agents interactions and routing requests.

## Overview

- How: Unified Services Level 2 Formation
- When: During Agent Provisioning
- Obligatory: Yes
- ORD impact: No

### Capabilities

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Integrating with AGW allows the Agent to:

- Call MCP tools through the AGW
- Initiate A2A communication through AGW
- Receive A2A communication from Joule through AGW
- Receive A2A communication from AGW (event-triggers)

## Quick Start

Use the SAP AGW SPII Implementation skill to generate the SPII endpoint, service, models, observer, and middleware for your Agent:

- [SAP AGW SPII Implementation](https://github.tools.sap/application-foundation/agent-skills/tree/main/.claude/skills/sap-agw-spii-implementation)

A complete working example is available in the [a2a-agent](https://github.tools.sap/agent-provisioning-test/a2a-agent) repository. It implements the full SPII lifecycle including Formation handling, Destination Fragment management, and MCP tool discovery.

> [!-info] -info
> About the example
> 
> The example repository also creates Fragments for a mock MCP server to demonstrate end-to-end tool discovery and execution. This is for **proof-of-concept purposes only** — in production, MCP Fragments will be created through proper System Formations with LoB participants.

## Steps to Integrate

### Step 1: Request Formation Access

Request to be added to the "Integration with Agent Gateway" Formation.

- Access: [CMP-15763](https://jira.tools.sap/browse/CMP-15763)
- Set the issue to `open`
- Add the following comment
```markdown
Please apply the following changes for onboarding our agent to the Agent Gateway formation type:

Application type: <your-application-type>

Required changes:
- Add the application type listed above as 'Initiator' to the formation type
- Enable SAP Cloud Identity Services (SCI) as Facilitator on both sides
```
- `<your-application-type>` = "SAP + Display Name" from onboarding form [issue](https://github.tools.sap/app-fnd-runtime/agent-onboarding/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) ". e.g. `SAP Sample Agent`.

### Step 2: Implement the SPII Endpoint

This SPII implementation follows the [Bi-directional SCI App2App Dependency Setup](https://pages.github.tools.sap/atom-cfs/atom-docs/docs/how-to-guides/integrate-your-app/use-sci-facilitator/#bi-directional-sci-app2app-dependency-setup). The Agent must implement the SPII endpoint to participate in the Formation lifecycle managed by UCL (Unified Customer Landscape).

**Agent Activities:**

- Agent implements the SPII endpoint (`PATCH /v1/tenantMappings/{tenantId}`)
- Agent informs the APIs to consume and to expose via `oauth2ResourceIndicator`
- Agent creates a Destination Fragment with the token exchange configuration upon Formation completion

> [!-warning] -warning
> Formation Type
> 
> The Agent must only accept the AGW formation type ID `d23d9e9a-fd1b-4dcd-b30b-01c4e86f4f8c`. All other formation type IDs must be rejected with HTTP 400.

![](https://pages.github.tools.sap/application-foundation/agent-runtime-domains/assets/images/agent-agw-tenant-mapping-b1a5dd666f5f648e478c3112a2bd6c3c.png)

#### Key files in the example repository

| File | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `app/api/spii.py` | SPII HTTP endpoint |
| `app/services/spii_service.py` | Two-step Formation state machine |
| `app/services/sci_app2app_service.py` | Token exchange configuration (oauth2ResourceIndicator) |
| `app/observers/fragment_lifecycle.py` | Destination Fragment CRUD |
| `app/middleware/mtls_auth.py` | mTLS certificate validation for UCL |

## How It Works

### What is provisioned by default

When the Agent is deployed, the Managed Runtime automatically provisions the following infrastructure:

- **Destination Service instance** — created for the Agent during deployment
- **Destination Certificate** — a new certificate with keys for a new Binding with the Identity service
- **Base BTP Destination** — a default destination, pointing to nowhere, with the certificate created above. This is used as a template and the Fragments created during Formation will update the destination URL and add the necessary headers for token exchange.

These resources are available out of the box. No action is required from the developer.

### What happens during Formation

When a customer creates a Formation between the Agent and the Agent Gateway through Unified Services, UCL notifies both participants. The SPII implementation handles this lifecycle in two steps:

**Step 1 — Initial configuration exchange:** both participants are in `INITIAL` state. The Agent returns a `CONFIG_PENDING` response containing its `oauth2ResourceIndicator` credentials (client ID, token service URL, protected resources).

**Step 2 — Ready:** the Agent Gateway is now `READY` and provides its own credentials. The Agent extracts the partner's configuration and creates a **Destination Fragment** containing the token exchange information, then transitions to `READY`.

The Destination Fragment stores the information required to negotiate **token exchange**: it enables the swap of a user token for an app-to-app token, which is necessary for agent-to-agent communication through the Agent Gateway.

### Destination Fragments created per Formation

| Fragment | Created when | Purpose | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **IAS** | AGW Formation completes (Step 2) | Token exchange for A2A communication | Available |
| **MCP** | System Formation with LoB | MCP tool communication through AGW | Coming soon — requires LoB/System Formations |

The IAS fragment is created automatically by the SPII observer when the Formation reaches `READY` state. MCP-specific fragments for LoB system integration will follow when Formations with LoB Systems and other participants become available. Formations with LoB Systems imply additional SPII waves to exchange system information and are currently under development.

### Key implementation details

The SPII implementation follows an **observer pattern** that separates protocol handling from infrastructure concerns:

- **`SPIIService`** — handles the SPII protocol state machine (validation, two-step flow, idempotency). Has no knowledge of Destination Fragments or SAP Cloud SDK.
- **`FragmentLifecycleObserver`** — reacts to SPII lifecycle events (`on_assign_ready`, `on_unassign`) to create and delete Destination Fragments.

The IAS Destination Fragment created on Step 2 contains:

```python
# Fragment properties
{
    "tokenService.body.resource": "urn:sap:identity:application:provider:name:sap-internal",
    "tokenServiceURL": f"{token_service_url}/oauth2/token"
}

# Fragment labels (used for discovery)
{
    "sap-managed-runtime-type": ["subscriber.ias"],
    "sap-managed-runtime-gtid": [global_tenant_id]
}
```

Fragment creation is **idempotent** — existing fragments are detected by GTID label before attempting creation. On `unassign`, all fragments matching the GTID are deleted.
